title: Kaze
description: Lying in the long grass in July, looking up past the stalks into a deep summer sky, and the wind is yours. Brush across the frame and your stroke becomes a gust: it runs on through the grass, the tall brome and seed heads lean over under it across the clouds and swing back with a little overshoot, and the clouds behind drift faster after it. Left alone, a light breeze keeps them moving.
intent: Technique 10, Kaze (factory/reality/techniques.md): an Eulerian motion field you author live. A 96x64 stable-fluids velocity grid (Stam 1999, https://www.dgp.toronto.edu/public_user/stam/reality/Research/pdf/ns.pdf) carries the air in metres per second over the whole frame; each cell's grass is a damped spring driven by dynamic pressure. The plate is a worm's-eye photograph from inside the grass, split in the bake into the grass alone (the sky unmixed out of every edge pixel, so the still recomposes to the photograph) and the sky behind it. The wind is drawn as per-blade bend: every grass pixel is displaced by the local bend times its lever (height above the roots below the frame, and how freely it stands), so stalks bend about their roots and cross the clouds. The cumulus drift is a two-phase flow map (Vlachos 2010), faster toward the zenith, and leans after the gusts. ?gust=demo throws a scripted gust, ?t=seconds runs the wind that long and holds it, ?breeze=0..2 scales the idle air, ?debug=bend overlays the bend field.

sources.author: Forest Service, Northern Region (USDA), via Wikimedia Commons
sources.note: Tall grass against partly cloudy skies, Tally Lake Ranger District, Flathead National Forest, Montana: camera at blade height pitched up. Display P3 converted to sRGB, worked at 2400x1600. Sky matte by tools/depth/segment.py sky (colour unmixing for thin blades), firmed by colour (sunlit brome is greener than the sky behind it) and darkness, and by a dark-object prior (a thin line clearly darker or greener than the sky inpainted behind it by a grey closing is all blade, so the brome crossing the sun stands solid); the sky behind thin grass is that closing, so the cloud texture runs on round the sun, which rolls off to warm white with its diffusion baked above a threshold; grass colour unmixed against a push-pull sky so a F + (1 - a) S recomposes the photograph. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/bake.py.
